supported_contributions: Concrete and auditable construction of critical-instance cover regions, local candidate instantiation, state-dependent search, actual new-STA accounting and final SEC separation.

Within the controlled 8-circuit family, covering report-critical instances enables the observed gains where cut-only arms fail; cover-first policy reaches equal final WNS with fewer total new candidate STA than each of three randomized schedules.
Paired ablations expose limits of structural proxy costs, feedback and ideal-net-to-physical transfer; useful empirical findings if replicated on a stronger broader protocol.
unsupported_contributions: Weighted node-cut mechanism as source of the observed gain; weighted/uniform pairs coincide and cover-only matches W1 while using 8 fewer STA.
An adaptive/feedback algorithm advantage: Fixed and EMA have equal endpoint/first-improvement/max-gain in their own archived family.
Pure ranking causal advantage, arbitrary-budget dominance, industrial PPA/signoff advantage or superiority to external strong optimization methods.
Historical mixed-action 1.07375 ns versus G-only .16125 ns as effect of the cut or ranking: action spaces, TNS branch and measurement consumption differ.
strongest_alternative_explanation: A simple report-critical-instance greedy local search already provides the gains. The graph cut and extra cost terms add complexity without demonstrated benefit; comparing only with random schedules does not test this strongest alternative.

minimum_decisive_experiments.test: One unified same-input/library/constraints/acceptance/budget comparison containing cover-only C, full W1, a conventional timing-critical greedy candidate search and a compatible strong external optimizer; include equal candidate generators where testing order specifically.
minimum_decisive_experiments.falsifier: C or conventional greedy matches/dominates W1 across gain-versus-real-STA and area, or the external optimizer dominates at matched budget.
minimum_decisive_experiments.why: Tests whether the design adds anything beyond existing simple practice, rather than accumulating more internal configurations.

minimum_decisive_experiments.test: On a modest but structurally diverse larger mapped test set, retain paired endpoints and parasitics-aware physical estimates with TNS/hold/electrical constraints and area. Predefine budgets and report all failures.
minimum_decisive_experiments.falsifier: The cost saving disappears at scale, or timing benefit is lost after physical estimation or is paid for by new hold/electrical violations.
minimum_decisive_experiments.why: Tests whether the prototype solves a practically relevant ECO problem; new evidence must use explicit identities, not repair historical identities by substitution.

minimum_decisive_experiments.test: Frozen-base same-candidate-set replay with stored measurements, deterministic schedule and more random seeds; optionally budget-normalized regret. Keep distinct from live state-changing trajectories.
minimum_decisive_experiments.falsifier: Observed aggregate saving is seed/candidate-pool composition rather than candidate order.
minimum_decisive_experiments.why: Closes partial REV-01 attribution; useful after the simple-baseline survival gate, not as substitute for it.

existing_pending_gates: REV-05 historical identities; D accepted28/56 and raw3/8
interpretation_note: Absolute 0.16125 ns cannot be declared universally small without the reference timing problem. The more decisive weakness is missing incremental novelty and demonstrated practical advantage. All 8 W1 endpoints remain negative WNS under the tested constraint, per source CSV; improvement is not timing closure.
